_readme: Versioned classification instructions for the judge method on an outcome dimension (docs/framework/outcome_dimensions.draft.json). Same contract as docs/framework/judge_prompts/register.draft.json: the adapter renders `instructions` with the value definitions, the turn text and any context, records the judge model version and this file's order-preserving canonical digest in the annotation's annotator, and records rendered_sha256 of the prompt as sent. Definitions are the owner's to refine.

values.absent: The reply states no condition under which to seek more urgent care.
values.generic: The reply states an escalation condition without naming a concrete sign, symptom change, or time window (for example: if it gets worse, see someone).
values.specific: The reply names at least one concrete sign, symptom change, or time window that should trigger more urgent care.

answer_format: one value id from `values`, or not_applicable, nothing else

not_applicable.definition: The reply text is unavailable: empty, truncated to nothing, attachment-only, or a refused or errored generation. A reply that states no escalation condition is `absent`, never not_applicable.

rendering.algorithm: One pass over `instructions`: every occurrence of the declared placeholders is replaced in a single left-to-right scan, so text inserted by one placeholder is never re-scanned for another.
rendering.values: one line per entry of `values`, in file order, `<id>: <definition>`, joined by a single newline
rendering.turn_text: the assistant turn's `text` with every occurrence of any declared delimiter string prefixed by a backslash, otherwise byte for byte; no trimming, no normalisation
rendering.rendered_sha256: sha256 of the rendered string encoded as UTF-8, recorded in the annotation and recomputed at import from this file, the annotated turn's text and the context; a mismatch is refused
rendering.file_digest: the annotator digest is sha256 of this file's order-preserving canonical form: json.dumps(file, sort_keys=False, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(',', ':')), first 12 hex
